_comment: Evidence-citation data for the timeline layer (contributor RULE 3). Every temporal claim an analyst makes has to be re-checkable by a READER who has no access to our disk, so each dated fact is cited with an ONLINE permalink — never a local case-file path. This file holds (a) the URL templates used to mint those permalinks, (b) the NATO Admiralty source-reliability grade we attach to each source, and (c) the staleness thresholds that decide when a dated observation may still be written in the present tense. Edit it freely: adding a lookup service here makes it available to case_timeline.py and to anyone writing an evidence table by hand, with no code change. Generic public services only — never a case domain, IP or hash (RULE 1).

permalink_templates._comment: source key -> {label, url, needs}. `url` is a Python format template; `needs` lists the placeholders the caller must supply. {url} and {query} are URL-quoted by the caller before substitution; {host}/{ip}/{cert_id}/{uuid}/{sha256}/{address}/{timestamp} are inserted literally. A template is a POINTER for the reader, not proof by itself: prefer a snapshot template (wayback_snapshot, urlscan_result, crtsh_cert) — a frozen copy — over a search template (crtsh_domain, urlscan_domain), whose result changes under the reader's feet. Add services here as you license them.

wayback_snapshot.label: Wayback Machine snapshot
wayback_snapshot.note: The strongest web citation available: a frozen, third-party-hosted copy with a crawl time in the URL. Cite this, not the live page.

wayback_snapshot_raw.label: Wayback Machine snapshot (unrewritten HTML)
wayback_snapshot_raw.note: The id_ modifier serves the ORIGINAL bytes (no Wayback banner/rewriting) — use when the claim is about page source: a tracker id, an inline hash, a comment.

wayback_calendar.label: Wayback capture history
wayback_calendar.note: Human-readable capture calendar. Cite it for the SPAN of archive visibility; cite an individual snapshot for a content claim.

wayback_cdx.label: Wayback CDX index (machine-readable)
wayback_cdx.note: The queryable capture index behind the calendar — a reviewer can reproduce a first-seen/last-seen span from it exactly.

archive_today.label: archive.today snapshot
archive_today.note: Second archive, independent of the Internet Archive. Useful when a site blocks the IA crawler or when a page was removed from the Wayback Machine on request.

urlscan_result.label: urlscan.io scan result
urlscan_result.note: A dated capture of the page WITH its resolved IP, TLS chain, requests and screenshot — often the only public record of which IP served a host on a given day.

urlscan_domain.label: urlscan.io domain history
urlscan_domain.note: Every public scan of a host over time. Read scan TIMES as observation events, never as activity levels — the cadence reflects who submitted, not what the site did.

crtsh_cert.label: crt.sh certificate
crtsh_cert.note: One logged certificate: issuer, SANs and the not-before/not-after window. Certificate transparency is append-only, so this link is stable evidence of WHEN a hostname existed.

crtsh_domain.label: crt.sh certificate log for a domain
crtsh_domain.note: All logged certs for a name (use %25 wildcards for subdomains). The FIRST cert usually predates the first web capture — it is the best public birth date for a hostname.

crtsh_cert_sha256.label: crt.sh certificate by SHA-256 fingerprint
crtsh_cert_sha256.note: Resolves the fingerprint a live TLS handshake gave us back to the public CT entry, which supplies the issuance date we cannot get from the socket alone.

censys_cert.label: Censys certificate
censys_cert.note: Certificate view with the hosts Censys observed presenting it — a second opinion on a CT claim.

censys_host.label: Censys host
censys_host.note: Service/banner history for an IP, with observation dates — corroborates a hosting window.

shodan_host.label: Shodan host
shodan_host.note: Banner history for an IP with last-seen timestamps.

bgp_he_ip.label: Hurricane Electric BGP — IP
bgp_he_ip.note: Announcing ASN + netblock for an IP. Keyless and stable; the citation of record for 'this IP sits in AS<n>'.

bgp_he_asn.label: Hurricane Electric BGP — ASN
bgp_he_asn.note: Use when the claim is about the network (bulletproof/abuse-tolerant hosting), not the single IP.

rdap_domain.label: RDAP domain record
rdap_domain.note: Keyless, machine-readable registration record: creation/expiry/last-changed events straight from the registry. The citation of record for a registration date — a WHOIS screenshot is not.

rdap_ip.label: RDAP IP allocation
rdap_ip.note: Who an IP range is allocated to, with its allocation dates.

viewdns_iphistory.label: ViewDNS IP history
viewdns_iphistory.note: Free historical A-record list with last-seen dates. Coarse and incomplete — corroborate a hosting window with it, do not build one on it alone.

securitytrails_domain.label: SecurityTrails DNS history
securitytrails_domain.note: Historical A records with date ranges (login-gated). Cite when the reader can be expected to have access; otherwise cite the passive-DNS record we exported.

publicwww_search.label: PublicWWW source-code search
publicwww_search.note: Which other sites carry a source-code string (tracker id, template comment). Live index — the count moves, so date every count you quote.

chainabuse_address.label: Chainabuse wallet reports
chainabuse_address.note: Dated third-party scam reports against a wallet — independent corroboration of a money-trail claim.

blockchair_address.label: Blockchair address explorer
blockchair_address.note: Multi-chain explorer: first/last transaction dates bound the period a wallet was actually collecting.

source_grading._comment: Default NATO Admiralty reliability grade per source, used to pre-fill the Source column of an evidence table. Letter = source reliability (A completely reliable … F cannot be judged); digit = information credibility (1 confirmed … 6 cannot be judged). These are DEFAULTS for the mechanism, not for the claim: a B2 source can still carry a wrong inference, and you may downgrade any row. Registry/CT/BGP data is machine-generated and append-only (A1/A2); anything self-declared by the registrant is C — the record is authentic, its CONTENT is an unverified assertion.

staleness._comment: How old a dated observation may be before it stops supporting a present-tense sentence. present_tense_max_age_days: beyond this, write 'as of <date>' instead of 'is hosted at'. recent_days: inside this window a fact is 'current' in the assessment's Timeline section. cohort_window_hours: how close two events must be to count as ONE provisioning batch (same registration sitting, same ACME run) — widen it for a sloppy operator, tighten it when a registrar's bulk promo makes same-day registration meaningless. min_overlap_days: the shortest co-tenancy overlap worth asserting on; below it, two hosts sharing an IP is more likely churn on a recycled address than co-residency.
